title: Fix the Array-vs-Pointer Type Mismatch
description: The program should point at the first element of an array and iterate through it.
actualProblem: &arr is the address of the whole array (type int(*)[3]), not the address of its first int element (type int*). Assigning it to int *p is a type mismatch that most compilers flag as a warning, and though it may happen to run on some setups, it relies on incompatible pointer types rather than correct, portable code.
explanation: An array name used by itself (like arr, without &) already decays into a pointer to its first element, with the correct type (int* here). Taking &arr instead produces a pointer to the entire array, a different and incompatible type.
